agentic.label: Works on its own
agentic.blurb: Can use tools and take several steps by itself — reading files, searching, running commands — instead of only replying.

coding.label: Writing code
coding.blurb: The people who made it publish it as a model built for programming; the claim and its date are shown on the model.

everyday.label: Everyday questions
everyday.blurb: Priced at the cheap end, so it is a sensible default for short questions, drafts and summaries.

long-context.label: Long documents
long-context.blurb: Holds a very large amount of text at once — a long report, or a whole folder of notes.

vision.label: Reads images
vision.blurb: You can attach a screenshot or a photo and ask questions about it.

uncensored.label: Uncensored
uncensored.blurb: The provider itself describes this model as uncensored — fewer content refusals. Its own claim, with the date we read it, is shown on the model.

frontier.label: Top tier
frontier.blurb: The vendors’ flagship models, grouped purely by price: every one of these bills at the top rate we list. Costing the most is the fact; being best for your task is not promised.

free.label: Costs nothing
free.blurb: Free to use right now — either your own hardware, or a free tier we checked against the provider on the date shown.

free.label: No charge
free.blurb: Nothing is billed for this one — the rate shown beside this label is $0.

budget.label: Low cost
budget.blurb: At the cheap end of what we list. The exact rate is printed beside this label.

mid.label: Mid-priced
mid.blurb: Between the cheap tier and the most expensive tier. The exact rate is printed beside this label.

premium.label: Priciest
premium.blurb: Among the most expensive models we list. Check the rate beside this label before you start a long job.
